findings.finding: The three LLM-facing nudge messages (level-1 repeat nudge, level-2 stronger nudge, and the manifest-FULL 'already in context above' nudge) are the steering content of this feature, yet the plan never states their actual text — only that they are 'static templated' and 'byte-stable'. The sibling steering surface in the same module (TOOL_STEP_STEERING_NOTICE, agent_call.py:38) gives its full wording inline; these nudges do not.
findings.location: Approach section ('first repeat... static templated nudge line; further repeats... stronger static nudge') + AC line 2 ('first repeat carries the level-1 static nudge, subsequent repeats the level-2 text')
findings.suggested_fix: Author the three nudge strings inline in the plan (e.g. as named constants), each including the cached tool name/signature template slot, so their wording is reviewable and the byte-stability AC pins real text.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Provide the exact level-1 and level-2 nudge template strings (or name the constant/module that defines them) so byte-stability is verifiable.
evidence: Plan: 'returns the cached result plus a static templated nudge line' and 'a stronger static nudge' — content never given
AC: 'first repeat carries the level-1 static nudge, subsequent repeats the level-2 text; both byte-stable across runs' — no reference string to compare against
findings.finding: The acceptance criteria require the level-1 and level-2 nudge lines to be 'byte-stable across runs', but the plan never states the actual nudge template text or where it is defined. An executor must invent the wording, and 'byte-stable' cannot be asserted against an unstated string.
scenarios: Executor writes arbitrary nudge text; a later reviewer cannot verify 'byte-stable' without an authoritative reference
findings.suggested_fix: Add the literal templates to the plan, e.g. LEVEL1 = 'This exact call was already made; the cached result is returned. Consider a different action.' and a stronger LEVEL2, defined as module constants in agent_call.py.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the memo cache's scope (per-agent-call vs per-run vs process-global), who creates it and when, and its retirement/clear path, so stale sentinels cannot cross run boundaries.
evidence: Plan says 'Add a memoize+nudge toolset wrapper at the shared agent-call seam' and keys on 'the EXISTING usage_log tool-call signature' but never states cache scope/lifetime
No CREATE/RETIRE path: who instantiates the memo dict, whether it is per-Agent-call, per-run, or module-global, and when it is cleared, is unspecified
ABSENCE: no consumer-staleness tolerance or eviction described for the cache
findings.finding: The memoization cache is shared state at the agent-call seam but its lifecycle (scope, creation point, and retirement/cleanup) is never specified. If the cache is process-global or outlives a single agent run, a stale sentinel like "(no matches)" could be served to an unrelated run whose repository state changed, serving a wrong answer.
scenarios: Two agent runs (or two turns) hit the same signature but the file changed between them; the second gets a stale cached result
A long-lived process reuses the cache across tickets and leaks memory
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the cache as per-Agent-call-instance (created when the wrapper is armed, discarded when the call completes), so no state survives beyond a single agentic run; add a unit assertion that a fresh wrapper starts with an empty cache.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.finding: The memo wrapper sits outside the steering boundary (guard->memo->steering), so a signature whose first execution was cached can be served the cached real result after the tool_step_limit is crossed, bypassing the steering convergence notice; the plan does not specify this interaction.
findings.location: Approach: 'wrapper order runaway guard OUTERMOST -> memo -> steering'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the memo handles identical calls within one parallel tool-call batch (same run_step) — e.g. cache the in-flight coroutine/future keyed by signature so concurrent duplicates await the first execution rather than all missing a check-then-act dict — so the 'exactly once for N identical calls' AC holds under batch concurrency, not only for serially-ordered repeats.
evidence: agent_call.py:91-95 guard comment: 'a parallel batch shares one step number, so only its first-observed call pays the O(window) ratio'
AC1: 'the wrapped tool function runs exactly once for N identical calls (unit test with a counting stub)'

The plan specifies no ordering/atomicity discipline (e.g. an in-flight future keyed by signature) for concurrent identical calls within one step; a plain dict get/set is a TOCTOU miss under batch concurrency
findings.finding: The memo is described as a signature-keyed cache short-circuit but the plan does not address duplicate calls that arrive in the SAME parallel tool-call batch (one run_step); a check-then-act cache lookup lets concurrent identical calls all miss and all execute, contradicting the 'runs exactly once for N identical calls' AC.
findings.location: Approach — 'Behavior: first repeat of a signature returns the cached result'; AC line 1
scenarios: Model emits a parallel batch of N identical read_file/search_files calls in a single step — all N miss the not-yet-populated cache and re-execute, so the counting-stub AC's 'exactly once' fails and the round-trip waste the ticket targets is not eliminated for in-batch duplicates

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State an explicit back-out mechanism (env/config toggle to disable the memo wrapper, or documented single-revert rollback) for this shared-seam behavior change.
evidence: Behavior change: 'first repeat of a signature returns the cached result plus a static templated nudge line' replaces real re-execution and alters message content the model sees
ABSENCE: no rollback plan, kill-switch, or opt-in flag described for disabling the memo wrapper
findings.finding: This changes existing agent-loop behavior at a shared seam: duplicate read-only calls no longer re-execute and the model now receives injected nudge text. The plan provides no opt-out/rollback mechanism (feature flag or back-out) if the memo+nudge interacts badly with a provider or degrades a run.
scenarios: Nudge injection perturbs provider prompt caching or model behavior in an unforeseen way and needs to be disabled without a code revert
findings.suggested_fix: Add a config/env gate (default-on) that bypasses the memo+nudge wrapper, and note the one-line revert as the rollback path; add an AC that the wrapper is inert when the gate is off.

Epic 9b71 AC: '...routed to a verdict built from fresh per-criterion evidence — never a bare LLMError' and 'budgets remain failure bounds, not workload ceilings'.

c827 comment: 'The earlier revision of this section said "withdraw tools so the agent lands a verdict on the evidence it has". That is superseded. ... the runaway's own context must not be the basis of a signed verdict.'

findings.finding: The leaf introduces a memoize+nudge deliverable (dedup cache + graduated static nudges that return the cached result so the model continues) that is not contained in either resolvable ancestor: the epic 9b71 ('detect runaways during the run, act, land a verdict from FRESH per-criterion evidence, never the poisoned history') nor the actuator ticket c827, whose comment history explicitly WITHDREW the 'steer the model to keep going on the same history' approach in favour of routing to a tool-free finalizer on fresh evidence. The leaf does not name its parent in its own text and no parent_id was supplied, so this is coached rather than treated as a confirmed contract contradiction.
findings.location: Plan under review: Approach / Behavior; parent 9b71-55b3-1bd1-4a97 Acceptance Criteria; parent c827-2a23-cd00-473e comment history ('WITHDRAWN'/'ROUTE TO THE TOOL-FREE FINALIZER — do not land on the poisoned history')
scenarios: A reviewer confirming the leaf is a subset of its true parent cannot verify containment because the parent is not identified in the plan text.
If the authoritative parent turns out to be c827/9b71, the memoize+nudge feature is out-of-contract scope layered onto a completed loop-breaker epic.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the prior-art survey to cite the existing memoize-duplicate-and-nudge prior art (e.g. published agent debounce/'DebounceHook' patterns) and the tool-call caching literature (ToolCache/ToolCacheAgent, tool-result-cache), then re-justify what is actually novel here (the specific nudge graduation + reuse of the actuator's shared tool-call signature at rebar's agent-call seam) rather than claiming no harness does this.
evidence: Plan quote: 'Research across agent harnesses (OpenHands StuckDetector, smolagents max_steps) found detect-and-terminate everywhere but no harness that memoizes the duplicate and steers the model back on course — graduated nudge-then-abort is the recommended pattern.'

Retrieved (DuckDuckGo): DEV Community, 'Why your AI agent loops forever (and how to break the cycle)' — publishes a seen_actions set that on a repeated hash_action returns observation {status:'duplicate', message:'You already called this tool with the same args...'} INSTEAD of re-running the tool — i.e. the exact memoize-duplicate-and-nudge pattern the plan claims no harness implements.
Retrieved (DuckDuckGo): AWS DEV Community, 'How to Prevent AI Agent Reasoning Loops from Wasting Tokens' — names a 'DebounceHook — prevents duplicate calls with identical parameters'.

Retrieved (DuckDuckGo): arXiv 'ToolCaching: Towards Efficient Caching for LLM Tool-calling' and OpenReview/SNU 'ToolCache / ToolCacheAgent' — established named work on caching deterministic tool-call results, which the memoization half of this plan reinvents unacknowledged.
OpenHands StuckDetector and smolagents max_steps prior art (the detect-and-terminate half) ARE corroborated by retrieved docs — that portion of the survey is sound.
OVERLAY basis: this is a novel-architectural-pattern bright-line; the plan itself frames the mechanism as unprecedented and cites a research survey to justify it.
findings.finding: The plan asserts its core mechanism is novel ('no harness that memoizes the duplicate and steers the model back on course') and that 'graduated nudge-then-abort is the recommended pattern', but retrieved sources publish exactly this pattern and an established tool-call caching literature, so the novelty framing is overstated and the prior-art survey is incomplete.
findings.location: Context / Problem — the 'Research across agent harnesses ... found detect-and-terminate everywhere but no harness that memoizes the duplicate and steers the model back on course — graduated nudge-then-abort is the recommended pattern' sentence
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer takes the 'no harness does this / recommended pattern' claim at face value and skips evaluating the published debounce+nudge and tool-caching designs for reuse or design lessons (invalidation, TTL, cache-key correctness).
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the 'no harness that memoizes... recommended pattern' claim with a cited survey: acknowledge published debounce+nudge patterns and the tool-call-caching body of work, note their gaps relative to rebar (no shared-signature integration with an existing distinct-ratio abort actuator; no byte-stable templated-nudge-for-prompt-caching constraint), and frame the contribution as the integration at the shared agent-call seam rather than as an unprecedented mechanism.

findings.finding: The plan's error-non-memoization mechanism keys on RAISED exceptions, but all four allowlisted read-only tools signal errors as ordinary string returns and never raise into the agent loop, so transient errors and honest '(no matches)' results would be memoized against the plan's intent.
findings.location: Approach / AC line 'Error results are not memoized: a call that raised re-executes'
findings.suggested_fix: Detect error results by return-value shape (e.g. leading 'Error:' from the fs tools) rather than by exception, and state explicitly whether a deterministic '(no matches)' is memoized-with-nudge (correct dedup) or exempted; update AC4 to test the string-error passthrough path, since a counting-stub that raises will not exercise real tool behavior.

findings.finding: The in-context nudge branch and AC line 6 depend on a pre-loading sibling's 'manifest' with FULL/skeleton file markers, but neither the plan nor the repo defines that manifest's shape, the FULL/skeleton marker vocabulary, or the API by which the memo wrapper reads it — and the plan states this ticket ships before the sibling. AC line 6 nonetheless mandates a unit test 'with a manifest marking a file FULL', which is unconstructable without a defined manifest type.
findings.location: Approach section ('In-context nudge for pre-loaded files: when the pre-loading sibling's manifest marks a file FULL...') + AC line 6
findings.suggested_fix: Either specify a minimal manifest-lookup seam this ticket owns (e.g. a callable returning a per-path marker from {FULL, skeleton}) that the sibling later populates, or restate AC line 6 as manifest-absent-only for this ticket and defer the FULL-branch test to the pre-loading sibling.
